key_insight: A symmetry-aware single-orbital tight-binding model can reproduce the low-energy band structure, spin splittings, and spin polarization of chiral 1D perovskite (R/S-PEA)PbI3 using only a small set of effective hopping terms.
engineering_relevance: This gives a compact, physically interpretable model for designing and analyzing spin, optical, and transport behavior in chiral lead-halide perovskites relevant to next-generation solar-cell and spintronic devices.
method: Built a single-orbital effective Hamiltonian on four symmetry-related sites per unit cell.
Included layer, in-plane sublattice, and spin degrees of freedom with separate parameter sets for conduction and valence bands.
Analyzed degeneracies using screw eigenvalues and antiunitary symmetries to distinguish accidental from symmetry-enforced features.
evidence_signal: The model was benchmarked against density-functional-theory band dispersions and was reported to quantitatively capture the band-edge spin splitting and leading spin-polarization patterns.
watch_item: Because the model is tuned to the low-energy band edges, it may not reliably describe higher-energy states or effects outside the fitted symmetry-adapted hopping terms.
paper_title: Single-orbital tight-binding model for chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites
